instruction.text: Read the description of Bernard Marx, a character from Huxley's novel Brave New World. Decide which of Maslow's needs are fulfilled and which aren't.

hint.text: Im Abitur werden dir Aufgaben begegnen, bei denen du bekanntes Wissen auf einen dir unbekannten Text anwenden sollst.
hint.label: Skill

atoms.text: Bernard Marx is an Alpha Plus (member of the highest caste) who often feels like an outsider in the World State. Physically smaller than others of his caste, he experiences insecurity and isolation — both socially and emotionally. Although he enjoys material comfort and physical safety provided by the World State, his deeper needs remain unfulfilled. Bernard craves belonging and recognition, but the society around him discourages individuality and emotional closeness. He envies others’ confidence but secretly despises their conformity. When Bernard meets John, the “Savage,” he briefly believes he has found a way to gain respect and a sense of importance. However, his self-esteem still depends on how others see him. He doesn’t truly reach self-actualisation because he cannot free himself from society’s superficial values. Bernard’s inner conflict shows that a person’s higher needs — belonging, esteem, and self-fulfilment — cannot be satisfied in a world that denies individuality and authentic emotions.

atoms.a: Which of Maslow's needs are fulfilled?

instruction.text: Decide whether the statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Bernard has to worry about food, shelter, comfort — they are not provided by the World State.
The World State guarantees stability, no war or poverty.
Bernard never feels isolated, different, and emotionally disconnected.
Bernard gains temporary recognition but still lacks true self-respect.
Bernard is able to develop his own identity or independent purpose.

atoms.b: Bernard’s story illustrates that even in a society that perfectly meets ((++material_and_physical independence_and_esteem)) needs, humans can feel ((++incomplete whole)) if they lack emotional depth and personal ((++meaning belongings)).

His frustration proves that self-fulfilment — the ((++top bottom)) of Maslow’s pyramid — depends on ((++freedom_of_thought mind_control)) and authentic relationships, not on social conditioning or external approval.
